versions.short: The bill would let the Interior Department extend certain existing National Park concession leases without going through the usual rebidding steps, as long as the operator has held the lease for at least five years, is following its terms, and the department finds the extension serves the park well. Before extending, the department would have to seek competing offers for 60 days and rebid the lease if a rival offer would give better terms. Extensions longer than 10 years would require notifying certain congressional committees 30 days in advance. The department would also be required to review each extended lease at its midpoint and could end it for noncompliance. Separately, the bill would allow leases of up to 99 years for redevelopment projects expected to cost more than $100,000,000, with notice to Congress 60 days in advance for leases longer than 60 years. Finally, the department would have to update its regulations within 90 days of enactment to reflect these new authorities.
